rounds.proof_sketch: The kernel is launched with blocks_per_grid = batch_size = 16. Therefore blockIdx.x (which becomes batch_idx) ranges from 0 to 15 inclusive. Original guard: batch_idx >= 16 is always FALSE. Mutated guard: batch_idx > 16 is always FALSE. Both guards evaluate identically (FALSE) for all possible executions.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the boundary guard from `batch_idx >= batch_size` to `batch_idx > batch_size`. However, this guard is dead code under the fixed-shape contract. The kernel launch configuration sets `blocks_per_grid = batch_size`, meaning CUDA will launch exactly 16 blocks with indices 0-15. Since `batch_idx = blockIdx.x`, it can only take values in [0, 15]. Neither `batch_idx >= 16` nor `batch_idx > 16` can ever be true when batch_idx is at most 15. Both conditions always evaluate to FALSE, so both versions process all 16 batches identically.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The guard condition protects against block indices exceeding batch_size, but CUDA's block scheduling guarantees blockIdx.x is always in [0, blocks_per_grid-1]. Since blocks_per_grid equals batch_size, no block can ever have batch_idx >= batch_size or batch_idx > batch_size. Both predicates are unreachable.
rounds.recommendations: When writing boundary guards in CUDA kernels, recognize that guards on blockIdx relative to grid dimensions are often redundant when the grid is sized exactly to the work. Such guards are only necessary when the grid might be over-provisioned (e.g., rounding up to multiples). Mutation testing tools should have static rules to recognize when block index guards are provably unreachable based on launch configuration.
